evidence: desktop_daemon.py owns only process lifecycle and state.
dimensions.recommendation: Keep API behavior in api.py and lifecycle in the manager.

evidence: The daemon composes the existing serve command and health endpoint.
dimensions.recommendation: Do not fork a daemon-specific runtime.

evidence: Start, stop, and status are closed CLI commands with bounded host and port inputs.
dimensions.recommendation: Keep internal instance identifiers hidden from normal serve help.

evidence: RuntimeDB retains application data ownership; daemon.json owns only process identity.
dimensions.recommendation: Never persist API tokens in daemon state.

evidence: Strict state, stale cleanup, binding policy, health identity, API behavior, and a real Windows lifecycle are tested.
dimensions.recommendation: Retain deterministic tests separate from the live rehearsal.

evidence: Failed readiness terminates the child; live identity mismatch refuses PID signaling.
dimensions.recommendation: Keep stop fail-closed on unverified live processes.

evidence: The daemon starts the provider-independent API and does not select or call a model.
dimensions.recommendation: Keep model lifecycle outside the daemon manager.

evidence: Later OS service integration can invoke serve directly without changing API or storage.
dimensions.recommendation: Add native service adapters only when platform requirements are explicit.

abstractions.purpose: Coordinate cross-platform detached process lifecycle and safe identity checks.
use_evidence: Used by all three required daemon CLI commands and the live Windows lifecycle.
complexity_cost: One state model, one manager, and one optional health field.
abstractions.recommendation: Retain until native service integration can reuse or replace this lifecycle boundary.
